raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year proper. I've been at this 28 years on these 6 mu — I'm not going to change everything just because somebody tells me to.

**My land and how I split it**

Main field is about 3 mu — that's where I run my cabbage-chili rotation. Spring cabbage goes in first, I pull it out in June, then I get chili transplants into the same ground for a summer-fall crop. It's tight but I've done it this way for years and the soil is decent from all the manure I've been putting down.

The other 3 mu I split — about 1.5 mu for eggplant (good cash crop, my wife handles most of the picking) and 1.5 mu for kidney bean. The kidney bean is partly for us to eat and partly for market. With six people in the house we need some food crops too, not just cash vegetables.

**Cabbage (spring, about 3 mu)**

I buy hybrid transplants from the same seedling guy in the county town — costs me around 80 yuan per mu but the germination is reliable, not like if I tried to raise my own. I transplant late February under plastic, harvest end of May into June.

For fertilizer I put down about 3000 kg of composted chicken manure per mu before planting (I get it cheap from the poultry farm one village over), plus a compound fertilizer — maybe 50 kg of 15-15-15 as base. Then I topdress urea twice once the heads start forming, about 15 kg each time. That comes to roughly 22-23 kg N per mu total. The extension guy came around a few years back and said I could cut back but honestly my yields are good and I'm nervous to change it. Last year I got near 5000 kg/mu which is a good crop.

Water: with well irrigation I give it 5-6 waterings. Pumping costs maybe 20 yuan each time, so that's real money but cabbage can't skimp on water or the heads split.

Pesticide: diamondback moth is the killer. I spray 3-4 times with whatever the agri-shop has — usually chlorantraniliprole now since the old stuff stopped working. Also a pre-emergence herbicide.

**Chili (summer, same 3 mu after cabbage)**

Right after cabbage comes out I rotary till and get chili transplants in — the window is tight, maybe 10 days. I buy the transplants, usually a local red variety that dries well because dried chili keeps and I can sell later when prices are better.

Fertilizer-wise chili is heavier than cabbage. I do base fertilizer around 60 kg of compound 15-15-15 per mu, then topdress urea three times through the season, maybe 12-13 kg each time. So about 28 kg N total. Plus I foliar-spray potassium during fruiting because my neighbor Lao Wang showed me his chili colored up better when he did that.

Irrigation: 7-8 times through summer. Chili is thirsty and hates stress during flowering or the flowers drop. Pesticides: aphids, thrips, and anthracnose. I'll spray maybe 5-6 times total. This is my biggest cash outlay after fertilizer.

Yield I'm hoping around 1800 kg fresh per mu, or if I dry a lot, maybe 350 kg dried per mu.

**Eggplant (1.5 mu)**

I transplant mid-April after the last frost risk, pick from July all the way to October. Long season, lots of labor, but good price if you can hit the market at the right time.

Fertilizer around 25 kg N per mu split across base and several topdressings — you have to keep feeding eggplant or production drops off. Compound base, urea and potash topdressings. Heavy manure base too.

Irrigation 8-10 times — eggplant wilts fast. Pesticide for red spider mite and eggplant borer, probably 6 sprays. Yield I expect around 4000 kg/mu if the market doesn't crash mid-season.

**Kidney bean (1.5 mu)**

This is easier. I plant in April directly from seed I keep partially — I buy some new seed every year to avoid disease buildup, maybe half and half. Beans fix their own nitrogen so I don't push urea much, maybe 8 kg N/mu just as a starter. Phosphorus and potassium matter more. I put down compound 15-15-15 at planting, maybe 30 kg/mu.

Pick fresh pods June-July mostly. Some we eat, some to market. Irrigation 3-4 times, pesticide 2-3 sprays for aphids and pod borer. Yield maybe 1200 kg/mu of fresh pods.

**Labor and money**

With six people in the house, family labor is our biggest asset. My wife and I do most of it, older kids help during transplanting and harvest. I hire maybe 10-15 days total across the year for chili picking when we can't keep up.

Cash is tight. Vegetables cost a lot to put in — seedlings, fertilizer, pesticide, pumping. I'm probably spending 8000-9000 yuan total on inputs for the year across all 6 mu. I keep some cash in reserve because if the well pump breaks or somebody gets sick, vegetables don't wait.
